terminal_record.title: State Department Visa Revocations Amid Crackdown on Foreign Student Activism
terminal_record.description_short: Supplied notes describe hundreds of visa revocations amid a campaign targeting pro-Palestinian students; they do not show every case was triggered by criticism of Israel.
terminal_record.description_medium: The supplied correction says the State Department, led by Marco Rubio, revoked hundreds of visas during a broader campaign involving foreign students and pro-Palestinian activism. It distinguishes the reported revocations from plans to screen social-media accounts and says some public descriptions referred to alleged Hamas support or protest activity. The packet does not establish that DHS revoked visas because of any post critical of Israel, or document the grounds in individual cases.
terminal_record.description_long: The frozen entry says the Department of Homeland Security began cancelling visas because their holders posted criticism of Israel. The supplied prior review narrows that account: it describes hundreds of visa revocations during a broader administration campaign focused on foreign students involved in pro-Palestinian activism, attributes the revocations to the State Department under Marco Rubio, and notes separate reporting about social-media screening. It also warns that public descriptions of alleged Hamas support or protest activity cannot be broadened into a claim that every person lost a visa for criticizing Israel. This draft keeps the agency and stated grounds qualified as supplied claims; it does not treat a planned screening process as proof of a completed revocation, and it does not present political censorship as a judicial finding. The packet includes no source URLs, individual visa notices, named affected cases, or readable excerpts establishing why any particular visa was revoked. It also does not establish a first effective date for the campaign, so the frozen March 1 date is not carried forward as a verified event date. The original assertions about students, academics, and professionals all being targeted, or every cancellation following social-media review, remain unsupported and are omitted. Before publication, direct reporting or government records would need to establish the relevant agency, dates, number of revocations, and the grounds cited in individual decisions. Until then, this remains an internal draft of the narrower account in the supplied notes.
